assumptions_made: The ScaleAI/fortress_public dataset was not suitable for equity returns analysis, so we generated synthetic equity returns that mimic real market characteristics including heavy tails and skewness
We used lagged returns as features to capture temporal dependencies in the return series
We chose 95th and 99th quantiles as representative high quantiles for tail risk estimation
We used Huber loss function in quantile regression for robustness to outliers
We standardized features to ensure fair comparison across models
We used a fixed regularization parameter (alpha=1e-4) for all quantile regressions
We evaluated VaR at 5% and 1% significance levels as standard practice in financial risk management
We calculated CVaR as the expected loss given that VaR threshold is exceeded
We used a simple scoring system to compare model performance based on VaR coverage and CVaR accuracy
We assumed that the synthetic data generation captured the essential statistical properties needed for this experiment
We used a fixed train/test split ratio of 80/20 to maintain consistency with typical financial modeling practices
We did not implement bootstrap confidence intervals due to time constraints, but the framework supports it
We used a simple linear model structure for both approaches to keep the experiment computationally efficient

results.hypothesis: To empirically evaluate whether quantile regression models estimated at high quantiles (95th and 99th percentiles) provide more accurate tail-risk estimates for daily equity returns compared to Gaussian error models, particularly when the underlying return distribution exhibits heavy tails or skewness.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Gaussian error model predictions for VaR and CVaR
results.success_criteria: If quantile regression models yield lower prediction errors (measured via VaR/CVaR backtesting) compared to the Gaussian model, especially during periods of high volatility or extreme events, the hypothesis is supported. Conversely, if there is no significant improvement or worse performance, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: Hypothesis not supported: Quantile regression models show worse performance than Gaussian model in tail-risk estimation.
results.methodological_validity: synthetic surrogate data — the pipeline is exercised but the findings are NOT interpretable as evidence for or against the hypothesis
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.
